slices.behaviour: Attempt 3 makes the evidence the amended criterion 1 names into something a reader can check rather than prose in a note. `harness run <ticket> --summary` now reports, per slice and from the journal alone, whether the slice was delegated and to which agent, read from the `--agent` declaration on the two checks the tdd record cites; the `--model` declaration beside what the route decided, so a slice that ran on something other than its route is visible; and the session's own output tokens with the subagents' apart from them, by calling `harness budget` rather than reading the logs a second time. `citations()` takes the latest citation per slice position across every tdd advance since the plan was accepted, rather than the latest record, because a rework round cites `position: null` and a reader that took the last record would leave a reworked ticket's slices with no checks. Nothing else in the summary changed, and it is still read-only. It belongs to no single slice: it reports on both of them. One repository convention was broken and caught by an existing meta-test rather than by a review: the new test class was defined after `if __name__ == '__main__':`, so a direct run of the module would have collected nothing from it. `GuardIsLastTest` failed the first regression at record 36, the class was moved above the guard, and record 37 is the green suite.
slices.failure_reason: `pytest harness/tests/test_loop.py -k RunEvidence` exited 1 with five failures, in the runner's words: `KeyError: 'slices'` four times, at the three per-slice tests and the not-yet-proved one, and `KeyError: 'spending'` at the session and subagents test. The sixth test in the class, that the summary writes nothing, passed before and after: it is what criteria 2 and 7 rest on and it was not supposed to move.
